artworks.title: The Rape of Philomela by Tereus
artworks.description: The rape of Philomela — Tereus' crime that starts the Thracian house's metamorphosis into nightingale, swallow, and hoopoe.

artworks.title: Philomela and Procne Preparing to Kill Itys (Athenian wine cup)
artworks.description: Procne and Philomela prepare to kill Itys — the sisters' revenge banquet before the feathers close the myth.

artworks.title: Tereus Confronted with the Head of his Son Itys
artworks.description: Tereus confronted with Itys' head — the recognition that turns the Thracian king into the pursuing hoopoe.

artworks.title: Statue of Procne and Itys
artworks.description: The statue of Procne and Itys — maternal grief cast in marble at the hinge of the bird-metamorphosis tale.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book VI — the tongue cut out, the woven tale, Itys served at the feast, and the three birds rising from the crime.

popCulture.title: Titus Andronicus
popCulture.creator: William Shakespeare
popCulture.description: Shakespeare's revenge tragedy rests on Philomela's loom — Lavinia's mutilation and the pie that answers Tereus.

popCulture.title: Philomela
popCulture.description: The silenced sister who weaves the truth remains Western literature's emblem of speech stolen and recovered in song.

popCulture.title: Procne
popCulture.description: The Athenian wife who becomes the nightingale — sisterhood, vengeance, and the feast of Itys.
